prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The first two frames place long merchandise shelves very close on the left and above the camera, roughly 0.3–1.5 m away, with the open floor extending several metres ahead and to the right. In the third frame, the depth map is dominated by a bright, apparently near region during the rapid turn, but blur and saturation prevent reliable distances; the fourth and fifth frames show a more open area ahead, with walls, windows, counters, and ceiling fixtures at roughly 2–8 m. The visible people in the last two RGB frames are several metres away, approximately 3–6 m, but their individual depths and mutual separation are not cleanly resolved. Compared with RGB, the map makes the near shelving versus distant floor and room boundaries clearer, while bright ceiling areas, dark voids, motion-blurred regions, and abrupt frame-edge changes look unreliable.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates three books and two bottles on the shelving in the second frame, all left-of-centre and above the camera wearer, likely about 0.5–1.5 m away and close enough to neighboring shelf items to be within tens of centimetres of one another. It also isolates one person in the fifth frame near the right side, several metres in front of the wearer; the mask is partial at the bottom, so the lower body is occluded by or below the counter/frame boundary. The masks make these object identities and boundaries easier to distinguish than in the cluttered or blurred RGB, but most shelves, products, counters, windows, and at least one other distant person remain unlabeled. Because detections appear only in isolated frames and several masks are incomplete, the map does not reliably support approach, retreat, facing direction, gaze, or arm’s-reach judgments across all five frames.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is entirely black across all five frames, so it provides no body or hand skeletons, facing directions, gaze cues, limb positions, or reach estimates. The RGB shows distant, partly occluded people in the later frames, but they are too small or obstructed for this map to recover their orientation or whether they face the camera wearer. Consequently, pose contributes no spatial information beyond revealing a likely detection failure, and it cannot track turning, approach, retreat, or interactions over time.
